newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel's Eisenach plant expects profits in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Opel's Eisenach plant expects profits in 1996.

text.p: German carmaker Adam Opel AG said on Thursday that it expects to report a small profit at its ultra-modern plant at Eisenach in 1996.

Manager Eric Stevens said the balance sheet at the Opel Eisenach GmbH unit, a showcase plant built on the ruins of a former East German factory, was moving in the direction of profitability, but added that payroll adjustments could have a negative impact on the balance sheet.

Stevens said that the carmaker, a subsidiary of the U.S. carmaker General Motors, will increase investment at the plant to around 60 million marks ($40 million) in 1997, around three times the amount invested this year.
Stevens said he hopes the plant will produce a model to replace the Astra in addition to the Corsa model it now produces.
The company said that it expected to produce around 162,000 vehicles in 1996, some 2,000 more than in 1995.
